C6-01-soil-composition-pie-chart

A pie chart showing the approximate composition by volume of a good loam soil. Four slices: mineral particles 45% (sandy brown), organic matter 5% (dark brown), water 25% (soft blue), air 25% (very pale grey-blue). Small simple icons beside each slice: tiny rock grains for minerals, a decaying leaf for organic matter, a water drop for water, a bubble for air.
C6-02-soil-profile-layers

A vertical soil profile in a cut-away pit, shown as a tall rectangle with horizontal layers. From top: a thin layer of leaf litter with grass and a small plant on the surface; a dark brown topsoil with many fine roots, an earthworm and small air spaces; a lighter orange-brown subsoil with a few long roots and small stones; a layer of broken, partly weathered grey rock fragments; solid grey bedrock at the bottom. A narrow bracket on the right side of each layer. Soft earthy colours.
C6-05-soil-sedimentation-measuring-cylinder

A tall glass measuring cylinder standing on a bench, containing soil that has settled into distinct horizontal layers after shaking with water. From bottom to top: a layer of small grey stones, a thicker layer of coarse light-brown sand, a layer of finer sand, a layer of smooth grey-brown silt, a thin layer of reddish-brown clay, then cloudy pale-brown water fading to clearer water, with small dark brown bits floating on the surface.
C6-06-soil-water-drainage-experiment

Three identical glass filter funnels side by side, each resting on a graduated measuring cylinder. Each funnel has a white cotton wool plug in its neck and contains a soil sample: left pale yellow sandy soil, middle dark brown loam, right reddish-brown clay. Water is being poured onto each from above (one small beaker shown pouring). The cylinders below show different amounts of collected water: most under the sand, a medium amount under the loam, very little under the clay, where a pool of water sits on the clay surface.
C6-07-air-soil-experiment-apparatus

Two-step set-up for finding air in soil. Left: a small metal tin with holes in its base, packed level-full with brown soil. Right: a large glass measuring cylinder holding water with the soil from the tin settling at the bottom, a glass stirring rod inside, and small air bubbles rising from the soil to the surface. An arrow from the tin to the cylinder.
C6-08-soil-water-humus-determination

Two heating set-ups side by side. Left: an evaporating dish of moist brown soil heated gently in a small laboratory oven at about 100 degrees, with a few wisps of steam. Right: a crucible of dry soil on a pipe-clay triangle on a tripod over a Bunsen burner with a blue flame, the soil glowing slightly with a little smoke rising. A small electronic balance between them.
C6-09-soil-capillarity-experiment-apparatus

Three identical tall glass tubes clamped upright on retort stands, their lower ends plugged with cotton wool and standing in a shallow trough of water. Left tube filled with pale yellow sand, middle with brown loam, right with reddish clay. Each tube shows a darker wet zone rising from the bottom: shortest in the sand tube, medium in the loam tube, tallest in the clay tube. A ruler beside the tubes.
C6-10-soil-microorganisms-experimental-apparatus

Two laboratory set-ups side by side. Left: two conical flasks closed with stoppers, each with a small open tube of lime water hanging inside above a layer of soil. Flask A holds dark fresh soil and its lime water is milky white; flask B holds pale heated soil and its lime water is clear. Right: a Tullgren funnel: a lamp above a funnel holding leaf litter and soil on a wire gauze, with a beaker of liquid below where tiny soil animals (mites, springtails, small larvae) have fallen.
C6-11-soil-organisms-ecosystem-block

A cut-away block of fertile topsoil showing soil life. A grass plant and a legume plant with small round root nodules on its roots at the top. Inside the soil: an earthworm in its burrow with worm casts on the surface, a few termites in a tunnel, an ant, a millipede, a mite and a springtail near leaf litter, a beetle grub, and a magnified circular inset showing rod-shaped bacteria and branching fungal threads around a root hair. Earthy soft colours.
C6-12-soil-erosion-types-stages

A three-panel illustration of soil erosion on a sloping farm. Panel 1: raindrops striking bare soil and splashing particles (splash erosion). Panel 2: a thin film of muddy water flowing evenly over a bare slope (sheet erosion) and small parallel channels cut into the slope (rill erosion). Panel 3: a deep, wide, steep-sided red-earth gully cutting through farmland, with a house and a palm tree close to its edge. Soft earthy colours with blue water.
C6-13-contour-ridging-terracing

Two side-by-side illustrations of a green hillside. Left: contour ridging, with curved ridges and furrows running across the slope following the contour lines, crops growing on the ridges, and rainwater held in the furrows. Right: terracing, a steep hill cut into flat step-like platforms with low stone walls at the edges and crops on each step. A small arrow showing the direction of slope on each.
C6-14-strip-cropping-aerial-view

Aerial-angled view of a gently sloping farm with long, curved strips following the contour: alternating strips of tall maize in rows with bare soil between them, and dense, low, leafy green strips of groundnut or grass. Small blue arrows show run-off leaving a maize strip and being slowed and stopped at the next dense strip, where a thin band of trapped brown soil is visible.
